# NOTES ON THE TWO BOOKS (for detailed Q&A; use instead of source text)

## BOOK 1: "The Little Princess of Tower Hill" by L. T. Meade (Gutenberg #38771)
Companion stories in same volume (not the table of contents): "Tom, Pepper, and Trusty"; "Billy Anderson and his Troubles"; "The Old Organ-Man". Publisher: A. L. Burt, New York. Illustrations noted: "I will knock. You are to say, 'Please is Mrs. Robbins in?'" (p.171); "I want to pick those white roses" (p.6); "I caught him my own self" (p.21); "Now, Jo, this is my cousin Maggie" (p.74); Maggie in contemplative attitude (p.91); "He put his arm around his little cousin" (p.158).

Chapters (titles): I Her Very Young Days; II Father's Short Visitor; III Snubbed; IV The Stable Clock; V The Empty Hutch; VI Jo's Room; VII In Violet; VIII Choosing Her Colors; IX A Jolly Plan; X A Great Fear; XI Going Home; XII In the Wood; XIII Thank God for All.

### Setting and characters
- **Maggie (Margarita Henrietta Villiers) Ascot**, ~7–8, "Little Princess of Tower Hill," only child of **Sir John Ascot** and **Lady (Beatrice, "Bee") Ascot**. Spoiled, saucy, blue eyes, curly nut-brown/gold hair. Insists on "Mag-Mag." Cannot read, write, tell time, or do figures. White pony **Snowball** (she later wants to sell him). Pink sash. Calls father "bairnie"-style pet names.
- **Nurse** (unnamed, petted Maggie; nephew "over-ripe" anecdote); **Grace**, under-nurse; **Thompson**, gardener; **Rosalie**, under-housemaid; **Jim**, stable-boy (smiles; teaches Maggie "pend'lum," "'and"); **William** (stable man); **Miss Grey**, gentle governess.
- **Ralph Grenville**, Maggie's cousin, son of Lady Ascot's sister **Mrs. Violet Grenville** (widow, "Aunt Violet"), Bayswater house. Ralph: brown-faced, slender, dark eyes, pompous grown-up talk, pets: fantail pigeons, pouters, rabbits **Bianco and Lily** (white, red eyes, given by Jo), horse **Raven** (black). Calls Maggie "muff" for getting up at 4 a.m. Ralph earns a penny a day when good.
- **Waters**, Mrs. Grenville's maid; keeps secrets "in violet"; ex-needlewoman.
- **Jo (Joanna) Aylmer**: crippled girl, lying on low sofa, violet eyes, fluffy hair, beautiful; "day-dreams" (wagon, fields, angels). Lives at Philmer's Buildings, Mrs. Aylmer's room (laundress & charwoman, no hall door, stone stairs).
- **Mrs. Aylmer**: laundress; husband (Aylmer) died of consumption; brothers **Ben** and **Bob** (twins; Bob has red hair), **Susy (Susan)**, ~10, thick-set, wants a tambourine (costs half a crown = 30 pennies).
- **Tom Jones** not in this book.
- Lamps/people at Tower Hill: "Janet" not here.

### Events in order
1. Maggie rebellious against Miss Grey (flings reading-book, wants roses). Nurse says brain "over-ripe." Sir John: "Miss Grey can't manage her." Lady Ascot: Maggie needs discipline; Sir John decides to send for Ralph.
2. Preparations in visitor's room (cricket bats, boxing gloves, racket-balls, little gun). Drive to Ashburnham station; Ralph arrives with rabbits, pigeons, fantails; Maggie catches rabbit herself.
3. Tea: Ralph patronizes Miss Grey; mentions Jo ("she's a girl"). Ralph/Maggie walk; Maggie pretends knowledge of clock. Night: Maggie wakes, dresses, wakes Ralph at 4 a.m. ("muff").
4. Maggie in garden; Jim at 6 a.m.; she asks time—"quarter-past six"; learns "pend'lum." She releases Bianco and Lily to eat lettuce; they escape into wood. 
5. Breakfast: Maggie confesses to father; Ralph angry-ish ("most girls are muffs; Jo isn't"). Mother summoned: Violet (Mrs. Grenville) telegram—Lady Ascot's sister gravely ill. Plan: children + Miss Grey go to London. Zoo/Madame Tussaud's talk.
6. London: Maggie visits Jo's room with Ralph & Waters; Susy and tambourine; Jo says she can "picter" the wood where rabbits went.
7. Zoo trip; Ralph explains Susy begs for bread; 14 pennies in hand, 16 more needed. Maggie cries; Waters comforts ("keep it in violet"); Waters tells her 14+16=30 by fingers.
8. Maggie sells her new best hat (white feathers, Perrett's, Bond Street) to Susy for tambourine; secret plan. Maggie's violet sash. Garden party invitation (Mrs. Somerville, Hugh's birthday).
9. "Jolly plan": books (Robinson Crusoe, Swiss Family Robinson, Sandford and Merton) as alarm; 3rd bang wakes her. Pawnbroker's shop: 7 shillings. Waters arrives, rescues; Susy runs off with money. Waters restores hat, scolds.
10. Ralph is kind; Mrs. Grenville says "you could have asked your father." Jo's home: Jo has fever, carried to fever hospital. Maggie catches fever from Susy; Ralph sent back to Tower Hill. Maggie delirious, talks of Jo, "country where grass is green, or heaven."
11. Sir John & Mrs. Grenville visit hospital; Jo near death; Susy begs at door. Waters at dawn at hospital: "You have got to live"; Jo: "tell her to meet me where the grass is green."
12. Maggie recovers; Ralph finds Bianco and Lily with nest of bunnies in wood. Sir John promises help.
13. Sept: Mrs. Grenville's cottage for new laundress—Mrs. Aylmer and Jo move in (Sir John's "deep-laid plot"). Maggie and Ralph take tea with "Mrs. Robbins"; Maggie reunites with Jo: kiss; "kindred spirits."

Ending line: friendship formed, "an episode... which was to influence all her future days." THE END.

---

## BOOK 2 of 2: "The Spring Song" by Forrest Reid (Gutenberg #76205), London: Edward Arnold, 1916.
Epigraph: Donne, "I am a little world made cunningly..."

Chapters: I The Beginning of the Adventure; II In the Lane; III New Arrivals; IV At the Window; V The Garden Door; VI Music; VII Questions and Answers; VIII Grey Weather; IX Pouncer; X Through the Darkness; XI Inspector Dorset; XII The Spring Song; XIII The Perfumes of Arabia; XIV The Recognition; XV Danger; XVI Grif Receives a Visitor; XVII Fantasy; XVIII Grif Awakens; XIX Doctor O'Neill Calls in a Specialist; XX Miss Johnson's Birthday; XXI Palmer at Work; XXII Fire; XXIII The Glittering Net; XXIV Grif Falls Asleep.

### Characters
- **Griffith "Grif" Weston**, ~13, sallow, sleepy-gentle, sensitive, sleepwalker, extremely sensitive to sound; hears "Spring Song" flute; walks in sleep. Dog **Pouncer** (bulldog; Ann says "Bouncer"). Parents travelling in the East.
- **Barbara** (12, prim, yellow side in croquet), **Ann** (10, fat, reddish hair, freckles, mouth open, loves Palmer, calls Edward "Angelina" mock), **Jim** (9, fidgety, riddles, "scout," with Pouncer; "Bags I"), **Edward** (15, fair, blue eyes, pointed chin, vain, smokes, at school; called "Angelina").
- **Palmer Dorset** (15-ish, sturdy, bright red wavy hair, freckles, small reddish-brown eyes; Sherlock Holmes-like; reservoir-nib inventions; revolver; "Balmer" to Ann).
- **Canon Annesley** ("grandpapa"), clergyman, writing book about fairies (Golden Bough); bald, black velvet cap.
- **Aunt Caroline** (Miss Annesley), tall, fair, letter-writer.
- **Miss Johnson**, governess, pince-nez, writing novel *Be True, Fond Heart* (hero Reginald; friend Victor De Lancy; heroine Angelina Ravenshawe; Maud Vivien).
- **Mr. Drummond**, curate, smooth-faced.
- **Clement Bradley** (= real name Tennant), church organist, silver hair, ebony stick, gold-headed; "Spring Song" (Italian, Gian Peruzzi); killed a man (brother) on a bridge; asylum; now tries to lure Grif; sings; Grif is his pupil.
- **Captain Narcissus Batt**, **Miss Nancy Batt**, **Miss Jane Batt**; red brick house by pond with cedars; grandson **Billy Tremaine** (William Batt Tremaine, died ~4 years ago aged 14; grave in churchyard; flute in his room).
- **Dr. O'Neill**, young doctor, car, bachelor; gives Palmer a small revolver.
- **Johnnie** (boy cleaning knives), **Bridget**, **Hannah** (servants), **Robert** (coachman).
- **George** / "Prairie Dick," circus man who stole Pouncer; shot in leg by Palmer.
- **Pan and Syrinx** (stable cats); tabby cat at Batts'.

### Events in order
1. June: train; Grif, Barbara, Ann, Jim, Miss Johnson, Pouncer travel to grandpapa's glebe house. Aunt Caroline meets them. Ann walks with Grif; meet Mr. Clement Bradley in lane. Grif chooses room near wood (window; swallow's nest). Edward and Palmer arrive; diphtheria at school. Ann/Palmer; "Angelina" episode; dinner with canon; riddles; Miss Johnson's novel synopsis.
2. Night: Grif at window hears wood-voices; flute. Pouncer sleeps with him.
3. Croquet tournament drawn: Jim/canon vs Ann/Palmer; Grif enters wood, meets Batts (Captain Narcissus and sisters); lunch; asks about Billy Tremaine room (not shown). Church: Bradley's music; Grif sings scales; "Spring Song."
4. Grif late returns; Miss Johnson complains. Batts/Bradley mention; Billy Tremaine's death explained.
5. Rain; Palmer's "raise the devil" story; play "Be True Fond Heart" performed (curate's hat sat on; Miss Johnson offended). Grif apologises.
6. Circus; Pouncer stolen by man with earrings; Grif chases circus by train to Rathcarragh, walks, sleeps by stream; Pouncer found; Grif sleeps in grounds of estate.
7. Palmer, Edward ambush George in tool-shed; Palmer shoots George in leg; canon keeps George; Dr O'Neill called.
8. Dawn: Grif with swans/dragonfly; flute by river; returns; Mr. Bradley accosts; Palmer finds Bradley's real name Tennant.
9. Grif's illness; Grif walks in sleep; Palmer nails window; Grif tells Palmer of "danger from a dead person".
10. Bradley's shadow-story to Grif (murder on bridge). Doctor and Palmer investigate Bradley's room (signatures, name Tennant). Miss Johnson's birthday (34); fire: Bradley plays organ, sets church afire, leaps from tower; dies.
11. Doctor reports to family; Grif taken to Batts; Miss Nancy shows Billy's room; Grif relieved; Grif "falls asleep" in Miss Nancy's arms. Ends: "But Grif slept on." THE END.

Also in volume: Arnold's publisher advertisements (Verdun to the Vosges, etc.), not part of narrative.
